q: How is IGVhope different from rent-to-own?
a:
Traditional rent-to-own arrangements often ask for an upfront payment and require additional monthly payments credited toward a future purchase. Depending on the agreement, these amounts may be lost if life changes and the purchase does not proceed.

IGVhope is different. There is no down payment needed to start living in your future home. You pay agreed monthly occupancy contributions, with annual increases capped under your agreement. The monthly payments do not include extra amounts set aside toward the purchase price, so there is no extra payment at risk of being lost. If your circumstances change during the ten-year term, your agreement sets out the options available to you.

Your purchase price is established through an independent valuation when your home is ready to move into. IGVhope is designed to hold that price from day one for the ten-year term. During this time, you can prepare to secure your own mortgage. When you complete your purchase at the held price in Year 10, with your own mortgage, then your home and any change in the home's market value become yours.

That is what makes the IGVhope program fundamentally different from other homeownership processes, giving certainty, time and support to own your home.

By Year 10 of your IGVhope journey, you will have established a strong occupancy payment history and received ongoing financial guidance, annual check-ins and support from mortgage partners to prepare you for homeownership. Throughout this time, your home's purchase price remains held by IGVhope from the independent valuation on Day One when you moved in, regardless of changes in market value. This gives you the certainty to plan for your future without chasing a changing housing market. The goal is for you to secure your own mortgage and complete the purchase of your home in Year 10, at your original held price. Once your mortgage is approved and the purchase is completed, ownership transfers to you. If you are not yet mortgage-ready as Year 10 approaches, the IGVhope team will work with you to review the options available under your agreement, based on your individual circumstances.

q: What if property prices go up or down?
a:
Too many future owners feel stuck trying to time the market, while prices keep moving as they save for a down payment or work toward mortgage eligibility.

IGVhope is designed to give you more certainty. From day one when you move into your home, your purchase price is set by independent valuation and held for the ten-year term. That gives you one clear price to plan toward, instead of chasing a moving market and feeling left behind.

IGVhope cannot predict the market. If your future home value goes up, the agreed purchase price still applies. If the value goes down, the ten-year period gives you time to prepare before taking on your mortgage.

What IGVhope gives you is time, clarity, and a known price to work toward.

q: What happens if I lose my job or cannot pay?
a: If you lose your job, experience financial difficulties, or need to exit the program, contact the IGVhope team as soon as possible so we can discuss your circumstances and the options available. Depending on your situation and the terms of your agreement, these may include short-term support, additional time to resolve payment difficulties or a managed transition out of the program. Your applicable legal protections remain in place, and any arrangements will be considered on a case-by-case basis. The program is not designed to remove all risk, and no housing arrangement can do that, but it does give you clear options and support when things change. Our team works through it with you one to one.

IGVhope is for people who can afford ongoing monthly housing costs but face barriers qualifying for a mortgage or saving the down payment needed to buy a home. You do not need perfect credit to apply. Eligibility is based on several factors, including stable income, your ability to meet monthly occupancy contributions and a basic credit check similar to a rental application. Some communities may also have local employment or residency requirements.

IGVhope is not emergency housing or a social housing program. It is a structured process to homeownership for people who are financially able to maintain a home but need more time to prepare for a mortgage. Register today and we will send you a short check-in to help work out if IGVhope could work for you. Whether you are ready now or on your way, the IGVhope community can support you with information and steps to strengthen your position toward owning your home.

Occupancy contributions are the monthly payments you make while you live in your home. Your monthly payments are aligned to the cost of holding the property, held by the not-for-profit housing association. They are set out in your Occupancy Agreement at the beginning, with annual increases capped under its terms. This gives you greater certainty about your housing costs and helps you plan your budget throughout the ten-year term.

q: What is the cap on annual increases?
a: Your annual increases are capped at a rate that is agreed when you enter the program. The specific cap for your home is set out in your Occupancy Agreement, so you know exactly what your maximum costs will be each year. The rate does not change once it is set.

q: What happens if I want to leave before Year 10?
a: If your circumstances change and you need to leave the program, there is a clear process for this, written into your agreement. You are not trapped. You will not lose savings or a down payment, because there are none to lose. IGVhope works with you to manage the transition.

q: How long does it take to hear back?
a:
The forms you've completed tell us what you need and whether the homes we have now could suit you. If you tell us you're interested in a specific location and unit type, it will help us to tailor our next steps with you.

Our team then looks at it and replies within 3 business days. That reply confirms we have what we need from you at this stage and explains the next step: everyone who registered interest in that unit type and location is in our contact list. We will reach out to that list about three months before construction finishes to begin documentation. The months in between are yours to build financial strength, with the Homeownership course open.

q: Can I choose which home I live in?
a: Yes. You can select your preferred location and home type when registering your interest. Our team will review your preferences and advise you of available options, expected construction timelines and the next steps. Home selection will depend on availability and eligibility requirements. In the meantime, you can continue preparing for homeownership through the IGVhope Homeownership Academy.

q: What does my monthly payment cover?
a: Your monthly Occupancy Contribution helps cover the costs of holding and managing your home through the not-for-profit housing association during the ten-year term. This contributes to the costs of the not-for-profit housing association holding your home, including property management, property-related expenses, maintenance and repairs, while you just pay the typical bills like utilities you use. Your Occupancy Contribution covers your costs to live in the home while you are building towards owning it at Year 10.

IGVhope is based on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, with homes planned and underway in Port Alberni, Campbell River and Ucluelet. Register your interest to receive updates on new developments and upcoming home releases in your preferred locations.

We are working with municipalities to bring IGVhope homes to more communities across Vancouver Island, the BC Interior and eventually across Canada. If you would like IGVhope homes in your community, you can write to your municipality through a three-minute process on our website.

q: Who owns my home during the ten years?
a: During the ten-year term, your home is owned by a not-for-profit housing association. IGVhope is designed to help you be ready to complete your purchase and own your home. At Year 10, once you have secured your mortgage and completed the purchase at your agreed price, ownership of the home transfers to you.

q: Does my monthly payment build equity?
a: No. Your monthly Occupancy Contribution covers the costs of living in your home during the ten-year term, while you are building towards entering your mortgage and then owning your home at Year 10. They are not credited toward the purchase price and do not build equity. IGVhope does not require a down payment or set aside any portion of your monthly contributions toward the future purchase. This means there is no accumulated purchase contribution to forfeit if your circumstances change and you leave the program. Your opportunity to benefit from any increase in your home's market value comes when you complete the purchase at your price which was agreed and held from day one.

IGVhope is designed to make homeownership more attainable, rather than provide social housing. It is for households who can manage monthly housing costs but face barriers to buying a home through traditional methods, like saving a down payment or qualifying for a mortgage. IGVhope offers a structured, supportive ten-year process to help eligible households prepare for and transition to homeownership.

q: What if I can't get a mortgage at Year 10?
a:
IGVhope is designed to help you prepare for a mortgage throughout the ten-year term, with financial guidance, credit support, a record of your occupancy payments and early engagement with mortgage partners. This can strengthen your application, but mortgage approval is not guaranteed. Because no down payment is required and your monthly Occupancy Contributions are not credited toward the purchase price, there is no accumulated purchase contribution to forfeit if you cannot complete the purchase.

If you are unable to secure a mortgage as Year 10 approaches, the IGVhope team will work with you to review the options available under your Agreement, based on your individual circumstances.
